Truncation Checker

Catch files that got clipped mid-write.
SKILL · RUNS AUTOMATICALLY WHEN IT APPLIES

What it does

Runs a token-minimal, workspace-wide sweep for files that were truncated mid-write - clipped before the write finished. It is the detection backstop to the write-time prevention sweep: where prevention tries to stop a bad write from landing, this skill finds the ones that slipped through and tells you exactly which files need attention.

What it catches

  • Mid-word tails - text that stops abruptly partway through a word or sentence.
  • Missing structural closers - no </html>, an unterminated JSON object/array, or an incomplete Python file.
  • Empty files that should have content.
  • Trailing NUL padding left behind by an interrupted write.

Auto-fix vs. report

It auto-fixes the lossless case on its own: trailing NUL padding is stripped, since no real content is lost. Lossy truncation - where actual content was cut off and cannot be recovered - is reported, not silently patched, so you can rewrite the affected file by hand.

How it runs

It wraps the root verify-write.py --scan engine and drives the daily 4 PM truncation-daily-scan task. You can also trigger it on demand any time you suspect a file landed incomplete.

When to use it

After a large batch of writes, after an interrupted or crashed session, or whenever a file looks like it ends in the wrong place. The daily scheduled scan covers routine coverage; trigger it manually for spot checks.

How to trigger it

"run a truncation scan"

"check for truncated files"

"did anything get clipped mid-write"
